summary: Correct IELTS format with good traps in Parts 1-3 (corrected dates, rejected options, a full Saturday group). Part 4 is the weak point: almost every note repeats the lecturer's sentence word for word, so it tests catching a word rather than following a lecture. No wrong answer keys were found.
strengths: Part 1 has a real trap for nearly every gap: age 7/6, Saturday full, 4.00/4.15, 15th/22nd March corrected, goggles optional, main door closed, post replaced by email.

Part 2 MCQs are built the IELTS way: the speaker herself rules out the two wrong options before giving the right one; the matching box has two unused distractors (evenings only; closed for repairs - echoed by the broken lift).
Part 3 is a natural two-speaker academic discussion with paraphrased keys (underestimate / report less; non-students / people who aren't students).
Script lengths (631, 727, 790, 779 words) suit the real timing; answers come in question order.

issues.problem: Part 4 notes are near-verbatim copies of the lecture (34 'kept secret by cooks at royal courts', 35 'mixing ice with', 36 'patented a hand-turned', 37 'stored in buildings insulated with', 38 'made the cone popular'), so Questions 33-38 need no paraphrase recognition; the explanations themselves say the phrase is 'heard almost word for word'.
issues.change: Script cannot change (audio recorded), so reword the note stems instead, e.g. 34 'royal cooks refused to share their recipes: they kept them ______', 37 'packed in ______ to stop it melting', 38 'the St Louis fair turned the ______ into a success'.

issues.problem: Option B 'It will open on Sunday afternoons' repeats the speaker's exact words.
issues.change: Suggest 'It will open at weekends for the first time'.

issues.problem: Box option A 'has moved to the ground floor' copies 'moved down to the ground floor'.
issues.change: Suggest 'is now easier to find' or 'has changed floors'.

issues.problem: Several Part 1 rows (age, class time, medical form, entrance) carry no paraphrase, which is normal for Part 1 but keeps pair coverage below 80% for this paper.
issues.change: No change needed; pairs added where a real paraphrase exists.
